slides.title: Your IP. Your Local AI Stack.
slides.subtitle: Surface Laptop Ultra: local code, grounded answers, selective cloud
slides.notes: This deck was generated on this Surface Laptop Ultra by Qwen3-Coder 30B through llama.cpp, with no cloud calls. For Zava's roughly 150 developers and architects, the question is practical: can local assistants support sensitive engineering work while preserving a controlled cloud option?

slides.notes: The installed runtimes are llama.cpp build 11573, native ARM64 with CUDA, and Foundry Local with its CUDA execution provider. These are runtime options, not an assertion that every catalog model works identically in both. The catalog occupies disk storage; it is not a simultaneously loaded model set.

slides.title: Memory Views Are Not Additive
slides.takeaway: Installed memory, Windows visibility and GPU budget describe distinct views.
slides.notes: Never sum these values or label system RAM as dedicated VRAM. They are distinct views, not independent capacity pools. Model files, context caches, runtime allocations and other workloads affect practical fit. The pilot should observe actual memory behavior rather than infer usable capacity by adding reported figures.

slides.title: MoE Is A Specialist Workshop
slides.takeaway: Selected experts work per token instead of engaging every specialist.
slides.notes: Qwen3-Coder 30B is MoE with about 3B active parameters per token. Its Q4_K_M file is 17.3 GiB. Activating selected experts helps explain faster decode than similarly sized dense models. Sparse activation does not mean only active parameters need storage, and speed does not establish answer quality.

slides.title: Measured Decode, Not Guaranteed Specs
slides.takeaway: Single-stream results favor these MoE workloads; validate quality separately.

data.caption: Approximate single-stream decode; shared device; Local-AI-Bench, October 2026.

slides.notes: All throughput measurements are from Local-AI-Bench on this device in October 2026, on a shared machine. They are not guaranteed specifications or comparisons against other devices. Qwen3-Coder also measured about 0.13 seconds to first token. These observations compare decode behavior, not accuracy or equivalent task completion.

slides.title: Concurrency Needs A Separate Test
slides.takeaway: Use aggregate throughput for capacity exploration, not individual latency promises.
slides.notes: The right side recommends testing concurrency, not assuming concurrency improves individual latency. Qwen3-Coder 30B and Gemma 4 26B results are approximate Local-AI-Bench observations from October 2026 on this shared device. Aggregate tokens per second is not a per-developer rate, and the pilot cohort does not imply simultaneous streams.

slides.title: Size Bands Guide Model Trials
slides.takeaway: Parameter bands help plan deployment; they are not accuracy tiers.
slides.notes: These bands are planning estimates in parameters, not accuracy rankings or memory guarantees. Evaluate candidates on Zava tasks, considering quantization, context length, runtime compatibility and observed resource use. A larger model is not automatically better. The local catalog offers candidates rather than a promise of equal suitability.

slides.title: RAG Is An Engineering Librarian
slides.takeaway: Retrieve relevant passages before asking the model to answer.
slides.notes: Propose a local index over approved internal engineering documents. Retrieve passages within the developer's permissions, then supply that context to the local model. Source references support review but do not guarantee correctness. RAG supplies context at inference time; it is not the same as training the model on Zava's documents.

slides.title: Proposed Local Stack And Routing Boundary
slides.takeaway: Keep sensitive context local; gate cloud requests before transmission.

elements.label: Sensitive code and context remain local

slides.notes: This is the proposed pilot architecture, not a claim of already implemented controls. IDE requests use local inference for code generation; document questions add permissioned retrieval. Local inference uses llama.cpp or Foundry Local. The policy router permits only approved, nonsensitive payloads to cloud reasoning. Sensitive prompts must not silently fail over to cloud.

slides.title: Make Hybrid Routing An Explicit Decision
slides.takeaway: Task complexity alone must never override the IP boundary.

steps.label: Classify request
steps.detail: Identify sensitive code, CAD/PLM data and documents

steps.label: Choose local
steps.detail: Serve sensitive and frequent work on device

steps.label: Gate cloud
steps.detail: Approve nonsensitive payloads for heaviest reasoning

steps.label: Review output
steps.detail: Check code, citations and developer acceptance

slides.notes: Interpret this flow as routing policy checkpoints, not a requirement to send every request through both execution lanes. Sensitive tasks stay local. Heaviest reasoning may use cloud models only with approved payloads. If a request cannot safely leave the device, keep it local or stop. Local execution is not an air-gap or certification claim.

slides.title: Turn Device Results Into Zava Evidence
slides.takeaway: A bounded pilot measures workflow value alongside latency and acceptance.
slides.notes: Enroll 10 developers for two weeks. Agree task samples and acceptance definitions before starting. Record acceptance rate, time to first token, completion latency and developer experience, distinguishing code generation from retrieval and noting contention. Review routing behavior and answer sources. Set decision criteria with Zava; no success thresholds or productivity gains are asserted here.

slides.title: Approve The Technical Pilot
slides.takeaway: Commit 10 developers for 2 weeks; decide from measured evidence.

slides.notes: Request an engineering owner, participating developers and an approved task and document scope. The device has demonstrated local model execution and generated this deck locally. The pilot now tests whether that capability meets Zava's workflow needs. Expand only after reviewing observed results and IP handling, rather than treating benchmark throughput as a deployment guarantee.
